samples.summary: Read-gating AttachDocument makes the shared-PDF viewer's unconditional `initialRoot` seed an actual write by a viewer (the role-conditional seeding fix missed the PDF provider)
samples.evidence: `READ_GATED_METHODS` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:104, checkAttribute:280-282) now authorizes `AttachDocument` as a read, so a share-link *viewer*'s attach is allowed. `PdfCollabProvider` passes `initialRoot={initialPdfRoot()}` (= `{ comments: {} }`, packages/frontend/src/types/pdf-document.ts:14) unconditionally, including on the shared route where `readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"` (shared-document.tsx:699-709). The Yorkie SDK writes every absent `initialRoot` key inside `attach`, which is precisely why the PR made every other shared provider role-conditional (`docsInitialRootForRole`, `notesInitialRootForRole`, `boardInitialRootForRole`, `sheetsInitialRootForRole`, shared-document.tsx:974-1020, with tests asserting 'seeds nothing for a viewer'). PDF was not converted, so a viewer opening a never-commented shared PDF now creates `comments` on the document — a write from the one role that must not make them, and exactly the invariant this delta's own comments claim only a hand-rolled client can break. If instead the SDK defers that seed to the next sync, the viewer's `PushPull` carries verb `rw` and is 403'd, leaving the shared PDF viewer in a permission-denied sync loop; either branch is a defect on a normally reachable path.

samples.summary: `assertYorkieAuthEnforced`'s stated precondition (the webhook refuses a preview token's writes) no longer holds absolutely once attach is authorized as a read
samples.evidence: `assertYorkieAuthEnforced` gates the public template tier on the premise that "unless the auth webhook actually refuses that token's writes" a `previewToken` grants write access, and its concrete worry is that one edit per card returns every listing to the review queue. `previewToken` is a `viewer` share link (template.service.ts:374). With `READ_GATED_METHODS` ignoring attach's verb (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:104, 280-282), a client can carry a change pack in the attach itself — the residual the new comment acknowledges — and repeat it by detach/re-attach, so the write the gate is predicated on being refused is reachable per attach even on a fully enforcing deployment. The invariant an earlier, already-merged gate relies on is weakened by this delta and neither the gate's doc comment nor the enforcement doc reconciles it.

samples.evidence: `sideTokenInjector` calls `yorkieServiceTokenInjector(secret)` with no `expiresIn`, so the lifetime is the hardcoded '10m' default. The replaced `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv` used `process.env.YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN ?? '10m'` (yorkie-service-token.ts:77), which the two sibling scripts (migrate-yorkie-cf-ranges.ts:221, migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.ts:347) still do — a deployment that shortens that variable now has one script out of three ignoring it. Harmless in practice since the injector re-mints on 401, but the behaviour change is undocumented in the new usage text.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. PdfCollabProvider (pdf-collab.tsx:189-191) passes initialRoot={initialPdfRoot()} unconditionally, and initialPdfRoot() returns { comments: {} } (pdf-document.ts:14-16); readOnly is received as a prop (pdf-collab.tsx:178) but used only for UI gating (217, 292, 331), never for seeding. SharedPdfLayout computes readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer" (shared-document.tsx:699) and hands it to that provider (707-712), and this layout is reached for any pdf share link with no role gate (shared-document.tsx:914-926). Every other shared provider WAS converted to role-conditional seeding (docsInitialRootForRole 974, notesInitialRootForRole 992, boardInitialRootForRole 1007, sheetsInitialRootForRole 1020), with the in-repo comment at 964-973 stating the mechanism plainly: "The SDK writes every `initialRoot` key the document does not already have, on each attach — so a viewer opening a share link to a never-edited document created `content` and `comments` from their own client"; tests assert "seeds nothing for a viewer" (docs-document.test.ts:38-40, board-document.test.ts:8-10). No pdfInitialRootForRole exists anywhere in the frontend tree. The backend half is also as claimed: READ_GATED_METHODS = new Set(['AttachDocument']) (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:104) and needWrite = attr.verb === 'rw' && !READ_GATED_METHODS.has(method) (280-282), so the viewer's attach is authorized as a read and reaches the server, with the controller's own comment (99-102) naming "a change pack carried by the attach itself" as the residual. The only nearby guard, pdf-comment-store.ts:123-124 ("Seeded at bootstrap (initialPdfRoot); guard only for legacy docs"), is downstream of attach and does not prevent the seed. Either outcome — a viewer creating `comments` on a shared PDF, or a 403'd PushPull sync loop — is a broken invariant/wrong behavior on a normally reachable path, squarely in the correctness lane. Major.

finding.summary: Flipping the enforcement default to "enforce" denies viewer-role share links at attach, because AttachDocument always carries verb `rw`
finding.evidence: `isYorkieAuthEnforced()` returns true for unset, so any deployment that registers the webhook methods and configures nothing else now honors denials. But this repo's own integration test documents the verb behaviour it collides with: packages/backend/test/revision-history.e2e-spec.ts:371-383 — "Deliberately omits `AttachDocument` from the registered set. Empirically … `AttachDocument` always carries verb 'rw' — even for a brand-new local `Document` object with zero local changes … Gating it as the backend README's own walkthrough suggests would deny a viewer's very first attach outright". The documented registration walkthrough (packages/backend/README.md:211, packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:573, docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:201) *does* add `AttachDocument`. In `decide()` → `checkAttribute()` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:257) `verb === 'rw'` ⇒ `needWrite`, and `hasAccess()` line 293 returns `link.role === 'editor'`, so a viewer share link gets 403 on its first attach and the shared document never opens. The same hazard reaches `PushPull`: Yorkie derives the verb from `pack.HasChanges()`, and every mount pushes a change pack containing its `initialPresence` (shared-document.tsx:993 sets presence for the note mount; docs/slides/sheets/board mounts likewise), so a viewer's PushPull can also be classified `rw`. docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:270-283 states this exact risk is *unconfirmed* and that the mitigation is "the rollout must confirm viewer-link attach/PushPull requests actually carry verb `r` (watch the shadow logs) before flipping … =true" — this change removes that staged confirmation by making enforce the default while leaving the verb question open and the README's method list unchanged.
